rationale: Buying the successful retest, which is the one thing this desk's own lesson file told it to wait for. The 14 August morning lesson reads: exhaustion needs a level that HOLDS when tested, not a big liquidation number - wait for the retest to succeed, then buy, because the entry is worse and the trade is far better. That retest has now succeeded twice. First on the settle, when the 22:00Z bar wicked 46.3 points through 62,846.3 and settled 36.4 points back above it, the first published line to survive its test in four sessions. Second on the overnight, when price spent six and a half hours making a higher low at 62,991.0, a full 144.7 points clear of the line, and never went back to touch it. Positioning eased in the same window rather than building: the OKX long/short account ratio FELL from 2.29 at 00:35Z to 2.25 at 07:00Z, the first decline in retail crowding since 13 August and 0.09 off the day high of 2.34; funding eased from +0.00970 to +0.00871 percent for the 08:00Z settlement, so longs are paying less to hold; open interest declined only 0.63 percent against the prior window's 2.01 percent; and forced selling has effectively stopped, with 31,417 dollars of long and 15,182 dollars of short liquidations since 00:00Z against 5.25 million long over the trailing 24 hours. On the timeframes the 4H MACD histogram crossed POSITIVE at +2.06 for the first time this week and the 1H histogram improved again to +37.13. The tranche is 20 USDT and it is sized at 20 rather than larger for one reason: the daily chart has not changed at all. Price sits below the 1D EMA20 at 63,889.02, the EMA50 at 64,414.50, the EMA100 at 66,510.36 and the EMA200 at 72,194.31, and the daily MACD histogram is -150.15 and widening. Sizing to the confidence that can actually be evidenced is the single most reliably profitable habit in this file - it turned a wrong midnight call on 14 August into a six-cent loss and a wrong endday call into a three-cent one. The entry at 63,107.2 is also 260.9 points ABOVE the 62,846.3 invalidation and 307.2 points above the 62,800 band that holds the largest measured liquidation cluster on the map at 1,178,314 dollars, which is the deliberate correction to the eleven logged sessions of accurate levels and losing executions - buy above the cluster, not inside it. The futures book stays FLAT. The overnight box is only 198.1 points wide, it is Saturday with the ETF channel closed, and there is no edge that justifies leverage inside a coil this tight; the stance is expressed in spot, which is where a low-conviction, direction-agnostic tranche belongs.

message.text: You inherit a 20 USDT tranche bought at 63,107.2 into a successful retest, a spot core of roughly 103 USDT and about 93 USDT of cash, futures flat. Two levels decide your session and both are deliberately placed AWAY from the clusters, not on them. Below: a settled 1H close under 62,991.0, the overnight low, is the reduce - do not wait for 62,846.3, because the 62,800 band holds 1,178,314 dollars, the largest measured cluster on the map, and below 62,500 the window has recorded nothing at all, which is unmapped rather than safe. Above: a settled 1H close over 63,309.4 with open interest NOT falling is the re-add, and that OI condition has now gone untested for three consecutive sessions, so if price finally gets there, check it properly before sizing up. Three things to re-verify first: whether the long/short account ratio kept falling from 2.25 or turned back up toward the 2.34 high, whether open interest stopped declining or resumed shedding, and whether the 4H MACD histogram held its cross above zero at +2.06 - it is a hair's width and it will not survive a bad four hours. Also remember what day it is: Saturday, US cash markets and the ETF channel are closed through Monday, so anything that moves price between now and then is derivatives positioning alone, and the derivatives tape is currently doing almost nothing. And use the BROWSER route for OKX - the run proxy served bodies six and a half hours stale this session.

lesson.pattern: Waiting for the retest to succeed before buying, and buying above the cluster rather than at the level.
lesson.insight: This is the first session that acted on both corrections at once, so it is the first clean test of them. On 14 August midnight the desk bought a flush on the size of the liquidation imbalance alone, with 62,846.3 untested underneath, and the level broke three hours later. Tonight that same level has been tested twice and held twice - once on a settled close through a 46.3-point wick, once by a higher low 144.7 points clear of it - and only now is the tranche going on. The entry is 43.9 points worse than endday's exit and the trade is structurally better, which is exactly what the lesson predicted. The second correction is placement: the buy sits 307.2 points above the 62,800 band that holds 1.18 million dollars of measured liquidations, because eleven logged sessions show this desk's executions failing precisely where the clusters are. Worth watching over the next few sessions: whether the two together finally break the twelve-in-fourteen losing streak, or whether accurate levels keep producing losing trades for a reason not yet identified.
